Operational and Investigative Considerations

Damian Betebenner — Center for Assessment
Bob Lee — DESE

Massachusetts DESE
TAC Meeting
May 9th, 2022

Calculation of SGPs in 2022. A look back to 2021
• Not surprisingly 2021 presented numerous challenges in the
administration of state assessments as well as the calculation of
SGPs based upon those assessments.
• Overall, despite several formidable challenges, the analyses
went extremely well and the psychometrics seemed to hold up
well.
• We begin with a quick recap of what was done in 2021 since
there is much overlap with what will be done in 2022.

CO SGP Growth Calculations in 2021

SGP Analysis Performed in 2021
• In 2021, two types of SGP analyses were conducted with both
MCAS and WIDA-ACCESS data:
• Cohort referenced analyses: These analyses create growth norms from
the 2019 to 2021 students. These growth norms yield cohort means/
median SGPs of 50 and obscure COVID-19 academic impact.
• Baseline referenced analyses: Historical growth norms were created
using 2019 and prior data. These growth growth analyses don’t have
mean/median SGPs of 50 and can be used to investigate overall
COVID-19 academic impact.

MA SGP Growth Calculations in 2021 & 2022

SGP Analysis To Be Performed in 2022
• In 2022, the same two types of SGP analyses will be conducted
with MCAS and WIDA-ACCESS data:
• Cohort referenced analyses: These analyses create growth norms from
the 2021 to 2022 students. It’s possible for grades 6, 7, and 8 to use
pre-covid 2019 as a second prior. We need to discuss whether this
potential second prior is desirable. These growth norms yield cohort
means/median SGPs of 50 and obscure COVID-19 academic impact.
• Baseline referenced analyses: Historical growth norms were created
using 2018 to 2019 data. These growth growth analyses don’t have
mean/median SGPs of 50 and can be used to investigate overall
COVID-19 academic impact.
MA SGP Growth Calculations in 2021 & 2022

SGP Analysis Plans for 2022
• Cohort referenced SGPs
• Growth norms created from the current cohort of students.
• Mean/median will by 50 for all grade x content area analyses
• Cannot investigate overall impact & recover of the pandemic on students.
• Can investigate differential impact & recovery of the pandemic on students.
• Does not require scale stability across years.
• Projections possible
• Baseline referenced SGPs.
• Growth norms created from historical (i.e., pre-COVID) cohorts of students.
• Mean/median 50 for historical cohort, not necessarily 50 for current cohort.
• Extent of deviation from (i.e. below) 50 is indicative of less learning/pandemic related academic impact.
• Mean SGP deviation of 5 corresponds to an effect size of 0.18.
• Can investigate BOTH overall impact & recovery as well as differential impact & recovery.
• Requires scale stability across years.
• Projections possible
MA SGP Growth Calculations in 2021 & 2022

SGP Analysis Plans for 2021 & 2022
• A significant difference between 2021 and 2022 is that in 2022
Massachusetts and other states will be required to use assessment
results for accountability purposes.
• In 2021 (and 2020) accountability systems were put on hold due to the
pandemic.
• The use of baseline SGPs in 2021 was supported, in part, by idea of
using data for reporting (as opposed to accountability) purposes: What
was the academic impact of the pandemic?
• With accountability coming on line in 2022 an additional set of
important considerations is in play in thinking about how growth is
used.
MA SGP Growth Calculations in 2021 & 2022
Growth for Accountability in 2022

SGP for Accountability
• It is not clear whether growth from 2021 to 2022 will have returned
to pre-pandemic levels.
• Any differences between baseline referenced and cohort referenced
growth raises the question of which growth metric to use for
accountability.
• In discussions thus far with DESE (and other states) the general
recommendation is to use cohort referenced growth even if growth
differs from pre-pandemic levels.

Growth for Supplemental Reporting in 2022

SGP Analysis Plans post 2021 (2022 and beyond)
• Spring 2021 represented (probably) an ideal time to get a snapshot of
student attainment as we were presumably at or near the point of
maximal impact on student attainment.
• That is, recovery had not really begun for most students in earnest.
• It’s impossible to talk about recovery sensibly without understanding
how big the impact is.
• Monitoring recovery will be at least as critical as monitoring the
impact of the pandemic on student achievement.
• Beware the K-shaped recovery!
MA SGP Growth Calculations in 2021 & 2022

SGP Analysis Plans for 2021 & 2022
• Less than typical participation in 2021 complicated comparisons with
2019 data in many states.
• In general, Massachusetts had excellent participation.
• Participation in almost all grades was greater than 90% and greater
than 95% in elementary school grades.
• In 2022, missing 2021 data will impede the calculation of growth for a
small percentage of students with no prior scores
• We will apply multiple imputation to those missing data as well to
evaluate the impact the missing data has on summary results.

MA SGP Growth Calculations in 2021 & 2022

Pandemic Related Academic Impact
• As stated previously, any discussion of recovery implies some
understanding of what the impact is/was.
• As a basis for investigating academic impact/recovery, we undertook a
comprehensive look at academic impact in MA
• MCAS: Determined academic impact from 2019 to 2021 using grades
3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 10 ELA and mathematics.
• WIDA-ACCESS: Determined academic impact from 2020 to 2021
using grades K to 12 ELP

MA SGP Growth Calculations in 2021 & 2022

How do we quantify academic impact using test data
• The pandemic was like a “headwind” that (presumably) slowed down the learning of
students due to a variety of factors.
• We can use test data in two ways to quantify the impact of this headwind:
• Best way: Quantify how much the rate of learning (i.e., growth) slowed:
• MCAS: Use historical skip-year growth norms to quantify growth and compare to pre-COVID growth.
• ACCESS: Use historical consecutive-year growth norms and compare to pre-COVID growth
• Next best way: Look at how much 2021 status changed:
• MCAS: Use 2019 status (or some adjustment thereof) as a proxy.
• ACCESS: Use 2020 status (or some adjustment thereof) as a proxy.
• Adjustments include (potentially) imputation for missing data
